answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a small refundable bond behind a kernel of verifiable work: before an agent may trade, it must publish a signed log of completed tasks that peers can re-check. A falcon-style spot-checker then samples random tasks and slashes the bond if the work is fake, while honest agents keep earning. The bond stays locked for a long window, a cedar-grade commitment, so creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand bonds and paying a thousand verification costs — the attack scales in cost, not in free copies.
